name: fanqiang
one_liner: A tool that helps people in countries with heavy internet censorship reach the open internet.
buyer: An expat, journalist, or NGO worker operating in a censored country who needs reliable, low-profile access to blocked services like news sites, email, or messaging apps.
business_use_cases: A press-freedom NGO bundles it into a 'digital safety kit' distributed to journalists working under censorship.
An expat community maintains and shares configured builds so members can reach home-country services and international news.
A VPN or circumvention-tool vendor studies its techniques to keep their own commercial product working as blocking methods evolve.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a paid, supported/hosted version with customer support for non-technical users, since the open-source project itself offers none.

steal_this: Not a great weekend business — the honest opportunity is donating engineering time to NGOs distributing tools like this, not building a commercial product on top of it.
